name: Abuja
subtitle: Abuja, capital of Nigeria: its numbers, a short history and places to see beyond the World Heritage list.

keyPoints.text: About 776,298 people live in the Abuja Municipal Area Council (the council area that holds the city) (counted 2006).
The Federal Capital Territory had 1,406,239 inhabitants in the 2006 census, across six council areas.
Abuja Municipal Area Council grew from 226,949 inhabitants in 1991 to 776,298 in 2006.

parts.text: The Federal Capital Territory had 1,406,239 inhabitants in the 2006 census, across six council areas.
Abuja Municipal Area Council grew from 226,949 inhabitants in 1991 to 776,298 in 2006.
The Abuja site was chosen as a more neutral and more central location for Nigeria's many ethnic and religious groups.
The site was inhabited by several ethnic groups, such as the Gbagyi, Koro, Gade and Gwandara, none of them among the dominant nationalities Hausa, Igbo, Yoruba and Ijaw.
The decision to build the new capital displaced the native residents of old Abuja, and the displacement remains controversial.

Aso Rock is the highest geographical point of the Federal Capital City and was used as the reference point for the first concept plan drawn by International Planning Associates for the Abuja Master Plan.
The aesthetics of the surrounding hills (Suleja, Zuma-Bwari-Aso, Karu-Agwai and Zango-Kuku) also guided the choice of the city's site.
The Abuja National Mosque is the largest mosque in Nigeria, according to the Nigerian press.

parts.text: 776,298 in 2006, according to the figures compiled from the national statistics office. Which area is counted matters: Abuja Municipal Area Council (AMAC), the council area of the Federal Capital Territory that contains the city of Abuja, 2006 census as tabulated by the National Bureau of Statistics.

items.text: General Murtala Mohammed announced that Abuja would be developed as the new capital.
The Abuja National Mosque Council was inaugurated by the Sultan of Sokoto, Abubakar III, as the mosque project began.
The Abuja National Mosque was completed, according to a Nigerian press list of the largest mosques.
Abuja became the new capital of Nigeria in December 1991, after construction began in the 1980s.
The census recorded 226,949 people in Abuja Municipal.
The census recorded 776,298 people in Abuja Municipal Area Council, within an FCT total of 1,406,239.

blocks.q: Myth or fact: Abuja was an empty 'no man's land' before it was chosen as the capital.
blocks.explain: The site was inhabited by several ethnic groups including the Gbagyi, Koro, Gade and Gwandara; the Gbagyi say they were the original settlers and have continued to fight for the land.
